porbos.title: The Treaty Quraysh Broke • The Fasting Army of Ten Thousand • The Cousin’s Return • The Fires of Marr al-Zahran

blocks.1: In the Treaty of Hudaybiyah the condition was that whichever tribe wished could stay with the Muslims, and whichever wished with Quraysh. The Khuza‘ah tribe was an ally of the Prophet {{1}}, Banu Bakr of Quraysh. One night in the eighth year of Hijrah Banu Bakr attacked Khuza‘ah, beside a well near Makkah. Quraysh gave them weapons, and a few, in the darkness of night, entered the fight themselves. The people of Khuza‘ah slipped into the boundary of the Haram, yet they did not get relief. ‘Amr ibn Salim of Khuza‘ah (RA) rushed to Madinah, stood in the mosque and asked for help in verse; we are your allies, yet they struck us down while we were in ruku‘ and sujud.{{2}}
blocks.2: Quraysh realised what they had done. They sent Abu Sufyan ibn Harb to Madinah to reaffirm the treaty anew. Abu Sufyan raised the matter before the Prophet {{1}}. The Prophet {{2}} did not answer a single word. He went to Abu Bakr (RA). Abu Bakr said, I cannot. He went to ‘Umar (RA). ‘Umar said, should I intercede for you? By Allah, even if I had nothing in my hand but a piece of wood, I would fight you with that. He went to ‘Ali (RA). There Fatimah (RA) was, and in front, little Hasan was playing. Abu Sufyan said, ‘Ali, will you intercede a little with Muhammad on my behalf? ‘Ali (RA) said, Abu Sufyan, the Prophet {{3}} has made a decision; I cannot spell it out. Then Abu Sufyan said to ‘Ali, what is to be done now? ‘Ali said, you are the chief of Banu Kinanah. You stand up and yourself declare protection among everyone, then go back to your home. Abu Sufyan asked, will this work? ‘Ali said, I do not think so. But what else can I do? Abu Sufyan stood in the mosque and announced, people, I declare protection among you. Then, mounting his camel, he went back to Makkah. Quraysh asked, what happened? He told them everything. They said, did Muhammad uphold it? He said, no. They said, then he was only playing with you!{{4}}
blocks.3: For the one who himself breaks his word, while running about to save the treaty, all doors are closed before him. Abu Bakr, ‘Umar, ‘Ali, none could do anything; because the Prophet {{1}} had by then already made the decision. Before breaking one’s word it is good to remember this day, the day when you will have to come back and say, what can be done now? The treaty for which at Hudaybiyah the Prophet {{2}} had returned Abu Jandal in chains, Quraysh did not let even two years pass; they themselves broke it. The one who keeps his word, in the end time stands on his side; the one who breaks his word demolishes his own wall with his own hand.
blocks.4: The Fasting Army of Ten Thousand
blocks.5: The Prophet {{1}} prepared quietly. In the month of Ramadan he set out with ten thousand Companions; eight and a half years after coming to Madinah.{{2}}
blocks.6: The preparation was so secret that even ‘A’ishah (RA) did not know where the Prophet {{1}} was going. The Prophet {{2}} had said to her, keep the household things in order. Abu Bakr (RA) came and asked his daughter, my daughter, what is this preparation for? ‘A’ishah said, by Allah, I do not know. Abu Bakr said, this is not the time for fighting Banu al-Asfar! Then where will he go? ‘A’ishah said, that I too have not yet been able to find out. So that people would think the expedition was elsewhere, the Prophet {{3}} sent a small party of eight under Abu Qatadah ibn Rib‘i (RA) in another direction. The news of that party spread all around. The real party was by then on the road to Makkah.{{4}}
blocks.7: Even in the work of truth not everything has to be told to everyone. The work for which the Prophet {{1}} had waited two years, even its preparation he kept hidden for a few days. Staying silent until the right time is part of wisdom itself. One Badri Companion had wanted to send news of the preparation to Makkah in a secret letter; that incident and the Prophet’s {{2}} forgiveness came in Dars 15. Everyone was travelling while fasting. Reaching a spring called Kadid the Prophet {{3}} asked for a vessel of water, held it up so everyone could see, and then drank in the daytime itself. After that, until reaching Makkah, he did not fast again.{{4}}
blocks.8: Allah had given the concession of not fasting on a journey. Yet many were fasting with difficulty. The Prophet {{1}} himself broke his fast and showed it before everyone, so that no one would feel shy to take the concession. For one who is a leader, one action of his lightens the hardship of many.
blocks.10: On the road to Makkah, at a place called Thaniyyat al-‘Uqab, two men wished to meet the Prophet {{1}}. One was Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith, the Prophet’s {{2}} cousin; for twenty years he had satirised him in verse. The other was ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah, a paternal aunt’s son, brother of Umm Salamah (RA); in Makkah he had said hard words to him. Umm Salamah (RA) interceded, O Messenger of Allah, your cousin, your aunt’s son, your relative. The Prophet {{3}} said, I have no need of them. The cousin tore my honour to pieces; the aunt’s son said in Makkah what he said. The news reached Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith. With him was a son of his. He said, by Allah, either he will let me come, or I will take this boy’s hand and set out, go wherever I please, until I die of hunger or thirst. Hearing this, the Prophet’s {{4}} heart softened. He called the two in. Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith (RA) came and said the very words of the brothers of Yusuf (AS), as the Qur’an has related it thus,
blocks.12: By Allah! Allah has favoured you over us, and we were certainly sinners.{{1}}
blocks.13: The Prophet {{1}} replied in the words of Yusuf (AS), as the Qur’an says it thus,
blocks.15: No blame will be brought against you today. May Allah forgive you. He is the Most Merciful of all the merciful.{{1}}
blocks.16: Then he recited a poem of his Islam and repentance. At one place he said, the day I carried the banner to make Lat’s horse win over Muhammad’s horse, I was a bewildered traveller on a dark night; today I have found the path. It was not I who guided me, someone else did; the one who brought me to Allah is that man whom I had driven away from every place. The Prophet {{1}} slapped him on the chest and said, you are the one who drove me out from every place!{{2}}
blocks.17: Twenty years of satire, all of it remembered; so at first he had even turned him away. But hearing of going out with his son’s hand to die, he could not hold out. At the time of forgiving he did not deny the hurt; he said this too, you are the one who drove me out, yet he drew him to his chest. To forgive does not mean to forget; it is to let go while remembering.
blocks.19: The army halted at Marr al-Zahran, close to Makkah. The Prophet {{1}} commanded, each of you light a separate fire. The valley filled with the fires of ten thousand people. Quraysh still knew nothing. Coming out to get news was Quraysh’s chief Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, with Hakim ibn Hizam and Budayl ibn Warqa’. Seeing the fires Abu Sufyan said, what is this! It is like the fires of ‘Arafah! Budayl said, it must be the fires of Banu ‘Amr. Abu Sufyan said, Banu ‘Amr are far fewer than this. The guards of the Prophet {{2}} saw them and brought them in. Abu Sufyan (RA) accepted Islam right there.{{3}}
blocks.20: The Prophet {{1}} said to ‘Abbas (RA), make Abu Sufyan stand in the narrow mountain pass, so that he sees the army’s passing with his own eyes. One by one the tribes began to pass, each with its own banner; Ghifar, Juhaynah, Sa‘d ibn Hudhaym, Sulaym. Each time Abu Sufyan asks, who are these? ‘Abbas (RA) says the name. Abu Sufyan says, what quarrel did I have with these! Then came such a band as Abu Sufyan had never seen before; the band of the Ansar, the banner in Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah’s (RA) hand. Sa‘d said, Abu Sufyan, today is the day of bloodshed; today even the sanctity of the Ka‘bah will be lifted. Last came the smallest band; the Prophet {{2}} and his Companions. Abu Sufyan (RA) told of Sa‘d’s words. The Prophet {{3}} said, Sa‘d has not spoken rightly; rather today is the day on which Allah will honour the Ka‘bah, the day on which the Ka‘bah will be clothed with its covering.{{4}}
blocks.21: The Prophet’s {{1}} green army began to pass. There, more than people, it was the iron armour that caught the eye. Abu Sufyan said, ‘Abbas, who are these? ‘Abbas (RA) said, the Messenger of Allah among the Muhajirun and the Ansar. Abu Sufyan said, by Allah, Abu al-Fadl, your nephew’s kingdom has become vast today! ‘Abbas said, Abu Sufyan, this is not kingship, it is prophethood. The Prophet {{2}} took the banner of the Ansar from the hand of Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah (RA) and placed it in the hand of his son Qays. The banner moved from Sa‘d’s hand, but it did not move from the hands of the Ansar.{{3}}
blocks.22: On the day of entering Makkah the Prophet {{1}} announced,
blocks.24: Whoever enters Abu Sufyan’s house is safe; whoever throws down his weapon is safe; whoever keeps the door of his own house shut is safe.{{1}}
blocks.25: The man who at Badr, Uhud and the Trench had come with armies, his very house was made a refuge. The defeated leader’s head was kept high instead of bowed; so that his accepting of Islam would not turn into humiliation, but become a door of honour.
blocks.26: Sa‘d’s (RA) words came from the anger of war; after twenty years of oppression such words coming to the lips is not unnatural. But the one who is the leader corrected his companion’s angry words, without shaming him. Today is not a day of revenge; it is a day of honouring the Ka‘bah. ‘Abbas (RA) said to Abu Sufyan (RA), now run to your own people. Abu Sufyan ran to Makkah and announced in a loud voice, people of Quraysh, Muhammad has come with an army before which you have no strength to stand. Whoever enters Abu Sufyan’s house is safe. His wife Hind came up, seized his moustache and cried, kill this fat one! What a bad bearer of news he is! Abu Sufyan said, ruin on you, do not fall for this woman’s deceit. Whoever enters my house is safe. The people said, how many of us will your house hold? He said, whoever sits with the door of his own house shut is also safe.{{1}}
blocks.27: Quraysh’s real reliance was Abu Sufyan’s word. Hearing such an announcement from the mouth of their own leader, no one else had anything to say. The tongue of that leader’s wife too was then fire. A few days later that same Hind would stand before the Prophet {{1}} and say, the honour of the people of your household is the dearest thing to me.

footnotes.0: Ibn Ishaq ← Ibn Hisham, al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah, ‘Fath Makkah’ (Banu Bakr’s attack, Quraysh’s help, the arrival of ‘Amr ibn Salim of Khuza‘ah in Madinah). Sirah-based. The part where the Prophet {{1}} said to ‘Amr ibn Salim ‘nusirta’ (you have been helped), al-Albani called weak (Fiqh al-Sirah, p. 373), so it has not been kept in the dars.
footnotes.1: Sirah-based: al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), pp. 648–650 (Ibn Ishaq’s narration). Sirah-based; the chain has not been verified in this dars, so it has come as a scene, not as evidence.
footnotes.2: Sahih al-Bukhari 4276 (from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas (RA); setting out in Ramadan, ten thousand, eight and a half years after arriving in Madinah).
footnotes.3: Sirah-based: al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), pp. 650–651 (the narration of al-Tabarani, Ibn Hisham 2/626–628, Zad al-Ma‘ad 2/150). Sirah-based; the chain has not been verified in this dars, so it has come as a scene, not as evidence.
footnotes.4: Sahih al-Bukhari 1944, 4275, 4279 (from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas (RA); breaking the fast at Kadid, raising the vessel to show people).
footnotes.5: Tawdih al-Qur’an, vol. 2, Surah Yusuf 12:91, p. 116 (Taqi ‘Uthmani, checked by rendering the PDF). The confession of the brothers of Yusuf (AS).
footnotes.6: Tawdih al-Qur’an, vol. 2, Surah Yusuf 12:92, p. 116 (Taqi ‘Uthmani, checked by rendering the PDF). The Prophet {{1}} replied in the words of this very verse (al-Albani, Fiqh al-Sirah, p. 376: hasan; see the next note).
footnotes.7: Ibn Ishaq ← Ibn Hisham; al-Hakim, al-Mustadrak (from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas (RA)). Al-Albani (Fiqh al-Sirah, p. 376): hasan; Shu‘ayb Arna’ut (takhrij of Zad al-Ma‘ad 3/353): the chain is good. Umm Salamah’s intercession, the Prophet’s {{1}} first refusal, the oath of going out with his son’s hand, the reply ‘la tathriba’, the poem and the slap on the chest are in this narration. The part about Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith speaking the words of Yusuf’s brothers (12:91) is in Ibn Ishaq’s narration, on ‘Ali (RA)’s advice; Sirah-based. ‘Twenty years’ is according to Ibn Ishaq’s narration.
footnotes.8: Sahih al-Bukhari 4280 (Hisham ibn ‘Urwah ← ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr). ⚠ This narration is mursal from ‘Urwah: ‘Urwah was a Tabi‘i, he was not even born at the time of the conquest of Makkah. Imam al-Bukhari brought it as mursal; Ibn Hajar said that most of it is established through other connected chains. The command to light separate fires is in Ibn Ishaq’s narration (Sirah-based).
footnotes.9: Part of the same Sahih al-Bukhari 4280 (making him stand in the pass, the tribes passing, Sa‘d’s ‘today is the day of bloodshed’ and the Prophet’s {{1}} reply). ⚠ ‘Urwah’s mursal portion; the sentence ‘today is the day of honouring the Ka‘bah’ al-Albani called separately weak because of its being mursal (Fiqh al-Sirah, p. 380). But the general announcement of safety for the people of Makkah is established in the connected chain of Sahih Muslim 1780 (the next note).
footnotes.10: Sirah-based: al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), p. 658 (Ibn Ishaq’s narration; in ‘Urwah’s mursal narration of Bukhari 4280 the banner of the Ansar and Abu Sufyan’s words are present; giving Sa‘d’s banner to Qays is in al-Rahiq, some have said it was given to Zubayr). Sirah-based; the chain has not been verified in this dars, so it has come as a scene, not as evidence.
footnotes.11: Sahih Muslim 1780 (from Abu Hurayrah (RA); Kitab al-Jihad, Bab Fath Makkah). Al-Albani (Fiqh al-Sirah, p. 377) also called it sahih through Ibn ‘Abbas’s chain.
footnotes.12: Sirah-based: al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), p. 659 (Ibn Ishaq). Sirah-based; the chain has not been verified in this dars, so it has come as a scene, not as evidence. This Hind bint ‘Utbah came a few days later to the Prophet {{1}} and accepted Islam (in the later part of the dars, Sahih al-Bukhari 7161).

quiz.q: In the Treaty of Hudaybiyah, whose ally was the Khuza‘ah tribe?
o: The chiefs of the Ghatafan tribe
quiz.e: Khuza‘ah was the Prophet’s ﷺ ally, Banu Bakr Quraysh’s.

quiz.q: Which tribe attacked Khuza‘ah?
quiz.e: Banu Bakr, with Quraysh’s help.

quiz.q: In the effort to renew the treaty, what advice did ‘Ali (RA) give Abu Sufyan?
o: To go to Abu Bakr and intercede again
To go to the Prophet ﷺ again and raise the matter
As a chief, to declare protection himself
quiz.e: Abu Sufyan announced it in the mosque; Quraysh said, he was only playing with you.

quiz.q: What is the lesson in comparing Quraysh’s breaking of the treaty with the Prophet’s ﷺ keeping his word at Hudaybiyah?
o: When you keep your word, time stands on your side
Making the treaty was itself a mistake
A treaty cannot be honoured from a weak position
It was proved that breaking a treaty is fine when one has power
quiz.e: One who breaks his word demolishes his own wall.

quiz.q: Someone has broken a treaty with me, though I had kept my word earlier; what does this dars say?
o: From now on I too will break
I will not make treaties at all
Keeping one’s word wins in the end
I will tell everyone and defame him all around
quiz.e: Quraysh broke it, and demolished their own wall.

quiz.q: ‘For one who himself breaks a treaty all doors are closed’; in which incident is this picture?
o: Abu Sufyan’s running about in Madinah
The reply to the Ansar’s weeping
quiz.e: Abu Bakr, ‘Umar, ‘Ali, none interceded.

quiz.q: How many Companions were in the expedition of the conquest of Makkah?
quiz.e: Ten thousand, according to Sahih al-Bukhari 4276.

quiz.q: In which month did the expedition of the conquest of Makkah take place?
quiz.e: In the month of Ramadan.

quiz.q: Near which spring did the Prophet ﷺ break his fast before everyone?
quiz.e: At Kadid.

quiz.q: Why did the Prophet ﷺ raise the vessel and drink water before everyone at Kadid?
o: So that no one would feel shy to take the concession
To show that the fast is not obligatory
To force the Companions to break their fast, as a punishment
quiz.e: One action of the leader lightens the hardship of many.

quiz.q: Someone in the family is struggling to keep the rules even in illness, though there is a concession; what should a leader do?
o: Shame them by sternly ordering them to break the rule
Take the concession himself and make the way easy
quiz.e: The lesson of raising the vessel at Kadid.

quiz.q: What was Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith to the Prophet ﷺ?
o: A relative on the in-laws’ side
quiz.e: A paternal cousin, who for twenty years satirised him in verse.

quiz.q: Who interceded for Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith?
quiz.e: Umm Salamah (RA).

quiz.q: In the words of which prophet did the Prophet ﷺ reply to the cousin?
quiz.e: ‘No blame will be brought against you today.’

quiz.q: On hearing the poem, what did the Prophet ﷺ say to Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith?
o: You are the one who drove me out
Your poem has turned out beautiful
Now recite another poem to me
From today do not write poetry
quiz.e: He said it, slapping him on the chest.

quiz.q: What is expressed in first turning away Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith and then accepting him?
o: He was compelled by Umm Salamah’s pressure
He was pleased on hearing the praise in the poem
quiz.e: To forgive does not mean to forget; it is to let go while remembering.

quiz.q: A relative who had satirised me for many years has come to ask forgiveness; what is the lesson of this dars?
o: Acknowledging the hurt and still drawing him to the chest
Humiliating him by recounting his old words before everyone
quiz.e: You are the one who drove me out; yet he drew him to his chest.

quiz.q: Seeing the fires of Marr al-Zahran, what did Abu Sufyan compare them to?
o: A forest fire on a distant mountain
quiz.e: It is like the fires of ‘Arafah.

quiz.q: Who else had come out with Abu Sufyan to get news?
o: Abu Jahl’s two sons and their men
quiz.e: Hakim ibn Hizam and Budayl ibn Warqa’.

quiz.q: Who was given the responsibility of keeping Abu Sufyan standing in the pass?
quiz.e: ‘Abbas (RA).

quiz.q: Who said ‘today is the day of bloodshed’?
quiz.e: Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah (RA), the banner-bearer of the Ansar.

quiz.q: According to Sahih Muslim, entering whose house was declared safe?
quiz.e: Whoever enters Abu Sufyan’s house is safe.

quiz.q: What is the significance of declaring Abu Sufyan’s house a refuge?
o: A strategy to keep him under watch
A plan to gather Quraysh in one place and imprison them
Protecting the honour of a defeated leader
quiz.e: So that accepting Islam would not become humiliation but a door of honour.

quiz.q: In reply to Sa‘d’s (RA) words ‘day of bloodshed’, what was the Prophet’s ﷺ position?
o: The day is not for revenge, it is for the honour of the Ka‘bah
Fully supporting Sa‘d’s words and becoming harsher
quiz.e: He corrected a companion’s angry words, without shaming him.

quiz.q: What could be the purpose of making Abu Sufyan stand in the pass and showing him the whole army pass?
o: To break the will to resist without bloodshed
To keep the army’s number secret
To punish him before sending him to Madinah as a prisoner
quiz.e: Seeing the strength, Quraysh gave up the thought of fighting.

quiz.q: The Prophet ﷺ himself was in the ‘smallest band’; what does this express?
o: A strategy arranged to deceive Quraysh
quiz.e: The biggest band was the Ansar’s; he was in the small band.

quiz.q: A leader of the opposing side has come over to my side; how is receiving him closer to the Prophet’s ﷺ example?
o: In a way that keeps his honour
Reminding him of his old mistakes
Seating him in the very back row for life
quiz.e: Declaring Abu Sufyan’s house a refuge.

quiz.q: Someone on the team has spoken harshly in anger; according to this dars, what should the leader do?
o: Correct the words without shaming him
Announce his expulsion from the team
quiz.e: The Prophet’s ﷺ conduct in reply to Sa‘d’s words.

porbos.title: From Three Directions, Among the Ansar • Entering with a Bowed Head • Inside the Ka‘bah • Standing at the Door of the Ka‘bah • The Adhan on the Roof of the Ka‘bah • An Exception to Forgiveness, and Restraint Within Forgiveness

blocks.0: From Three Directions, Among the Ansar
blocks.1: Reaching Dhu Tuwa the Prophet {{1}} drew up the army in ranks. The army would enter Makkah from three directions. On one side Zubayr ibn al-‘Awwam (RA), on another Khalid ibn al-Walid (RA). With the infantry, Abu ‘Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah (RA) through the middle of the valley. The Prophet {{2}} himself was in one band. Seeing Abu Hurayrah (RA) in the distance he called, Abu Hurayrah! He said, at your service, O Messenger of Allah. The Prophet {{3}} said, let no one come to me except an Ansari. Call the Ansar. The Ansar came and stood around the Prophet {{4}}. Meanwhile Quraysh gathered a rabble of its own. They thought, let us send these ahead. If they gain some advantage we will be with them. If they lose, we will give them whatever they want. The Prophet {{5}} saw them and said, do you see that band of Quraysh? Then, placing one hand over the other, he gestured, until you meet me at Safa. On Khalid’s (RA) path was Khandamah. There ‘Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, Safwan ibn Umayyah and Suhayl ibn ‘Amr had gathered to stop the Muslims. Himas ibn Qays of Banu Bakr had been making weapons for days on end. His wife had asked, who are these for? He had said, for Muhammad and his companions. His wife had said, by Allah, no one can stop them. He had said, I will make one of them your servant. There was a little fighting. Twelve of Quraysh were killed. The rest ran away. Safwan and ‘Ikrimah too. Two of the Muslims were martyred, Kurz ibn Jabir al-Fihri and Khunays ibn Khalid (RA), who had gone by a separate path from the main body and got lost. Himas returned home and told his wife, quickly bolt the doors and windows. His wife said, where has gone all that you were saying all this time? He said, if you had been there on the day of Khandamah, the day Safwan and ‘Ikrimah fled, you would not have rebuked me.{{6}}
blocks.2: The weapon made for the Prophet {{1}} and his companions was of no use on the field. Boasting with the mouth is easy. The weight is known when you stand face to face. And the hand that ran to stop the Prophet {{2}}, from that very hand in the end a pact of safety had to be asked.
blocks.4: Into the city from which eight years earlier he had had to leave, hidden, in the darkness of night, the Prophet {{1}} entered on camelback. Anas (RA) said, he entered Makkah with his chin resting on the howdah, bowed, in humility.{{2}}
blocks.5: And sitting on the camel he was reciting Surah al-Fath, drawing out the tune, repeating again and again.{{1}}
blocks.6: The surah in whose very beginning, about two years earlier, the Treaty of Hudaybiyah had been called a victory, on the day when many of the Companions could not understand it; today he enters Makkah reciting that same surah with his own mouth. At the moment of victory there is no proud announcement on his lips, there is the Qur’an; the head is not raised, it is bowed. What became of the Ka‘bah and the idols around it is told in Dars 2.
blocks.8: After finishing the tawaf the Prophet {{1}} called ‘Uthman ibn Talhah (RA), the keeper of the Ka‘bah’s key. He told him to bring the key. The door opened. But the Prophet {{2}} did not enter at once. Inside there were still idols and pictures. Ibn ‘Abbas (RA) said, the Prophet {{3}} refused to enter while there were gods inside. He gave the order, and they were brought out. Brought out too were the pictures of Ibrahim and Isma‘il (AS), with divination arrows in their hands. The Prophet {{4}} said,
blocks.10: May Allah destroy them! They know very well that Ibrahim and Isma‘il never sought to learn fate with these arrows.{{1}}
blocks.11: Then he entered. With him were Usamah ibn Zayd, Bilal and ‘Uthman ibn Talhah (RA). The door was closed from inside. He spent a long time inside. In the corners of the house he said takbir. Then he prayed. When he came out Ibn ‘Umar (RA), entering first of all, saw Bilal (RA) standing beyond the door. He asked, did the Prophet {{1}} pray inside the Ka‘bah? Bilal said,
blocks.13: Yes, two rak‘ahs. Between the two pillars on the left as you enter.{{1}}
blocks.16: In the house that Ibrahim (AS) had raised for tawhid, pictures were drawn in his own name, with divination arrows in the hand. People love to carry on the work they like in the names of great people. The Prophet {{1}} first wiped out that false name, then entered. Even entering as a victor, he did not set foot inside without stopping the work that had been going on in the house. Today in our houses too such pictures exist. A deed that was not to the Prophet’s {{2}} liking, yet is carried on by invoking elders: the people before us used to do it. Before entering the house those pictures need to be taken down.
blocks.17: Standing at the Door of the Ka‘bah
blocks.18: Then the Prophet {{1}} stood at the door of the Ka‘bah. Below were the people of Makkah; those who had thrown stones, who had starved him in the Valley of Abu Talib, who had plotted murder, who had laid the Companions on hot sand and put stones on their chests. Everyone was waiting to see what would happen. He said takbir three times, then said,
blocks.20: There is no god but Allah, He is One. He has made His promise true, helped His servant, and alone defeated all the factions. Listen, every pride, every claim of blood and wealth of the Jahiliyyah is beneath these two feet of mine; except the service of the Ka‘bah and the duty of giving water to the pilgrims.{{1}}
blocks.21: The chain of revenge of Jahiliyyah went on across tribe after tribe; the son took revenge for the father’s blood, the grandson for the son’s. In one sentence that chain was pressed beneath the feet. Then he asked, O Quraysh, what do you think I will do with you? They said, something good; you are a kind brother, son of a kind brother. He said, go, you are free.{{1}}
blocks.22: Twenty years’ account in hand, the witness of every blow standing in front. Yet not a single name was taken up for judgement. Power coming into hand usually changes people; he did not change; the kindness that was there in the weak days of Makkah, on the day of victory too it remained.
blocks.23: The Adhan on the Roof of the Ka‘bah
blocks.24: The time of prayer came. By the Prophet’s {{1}} command Bilal (RA) climbed to the roof of the Ka‘bah and called the adhan. From the throat that once had Makkah’s hot sand and a stone on the chest, there floated Allahu akbar. Where for a thousand years the market of idols had been crowded, for the first time rang out the adhan of tawhid. In the courtyard of the Ka‘bah some Qurayshis were then sitting: Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, ‘Attab ibn Usayd and al-Harith ibn Hisham. ‘Attab said, Allah has honoured my father Usayd, he did not have to hear this sound. al-Harith said, by Allah, if I knew he was on the truth, I would follow him. Abu Sufyan said, I will say nothing. If I make a sound these very pebbles will tell him. The Prophet {{2}} came to them and said, I have come to know all that you said. Then he told their words one by one. ‘Attab and al-Harith said, we bear witness that you are the Messenger of Allah. By Allah, no one was with us who could have conveyed this to you.{{3}}
blocks.25: However much a word is whispered, to the One who is listening there is no difference between a whisper and a shout. No one had informed the Prophet {{1}}. We keep a wall standing between what we say in hiding and what we say openly. That wall in fact does not exist.
blocks.26: An Exception to Forgiveness, and Restraint Within Forgiveness
blocks.27: There was forgiveness. But not every crime went on the same scale. Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas (RA) said, on the day of the conquest of Makkah the Prophet {{1}} gave safety to everyone, except four men and two women. He named them too. One of those four was ‘Abdullah ibn Sa‘d ibn Abi Sarh. Ibn Khatal was hanging on to the cloth of the Ka‘bah. Someone informed the Prophet {{2}}. He said, kill him. According to al-Rahiq, singing verses in satire of the Prophet {{3}} and the Muslims had been the work of him and his two slave-girls. ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Sarh had hidden with ‘Uthman ibn ‘Affan (RA), his foster brother. When the Prophet {{4}} called the people to the pledge, ‘Uthman brought him along and stood him before the Prophet {{5}}. He said, O Prophet of Allah, take ‘Abdullah’s pledge. The Prophet {{6}} raised his head and looked. He held back his hand. Three times. Three times he refused to take it. After the third time he took the pledge. Then he turned to the Companions and said,
blocks.29: Was there not even one sensible man among you, who on seeing me withhold my hand from his pledge would have stood up and killed him? The Companions said, we did not know what was in your mind. Why did you not signal us with your eye? He said, it does not befit a prophet to have a deceit of the eyes.{{1}}
blocks.31: Forgiveness does not mean abolishing the law. And within the law too the path of forgiveness was open. ‘Uthman interceded, the Prophet {{1}} accepted, though late. But giving an order to kill someone by a hint, one thing on the tongue, another in the mind, this posture is not for the Prophet {{2}}. What is in the mind is on the tongue. Keeping this match is the hardest of all. About several others on the list there are small stories in history. ‘Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl had fled on the road to Yemen. His wife asked the Prophet {{3}} for safety. The Prophet {{4}} granted it. The wife herself rushed and brought her husband back. ‘Ikrimah accepted Islam, and in his later life his Islam was very beautiful. Safwan ibn Umayyah’s name was not on the list. But out of fear he too had fled. He had decided to go by sea to Yemen via Jeddah. Just then ‘Umayr ibn Wahb (RA) reached him. The very ‘Umayr whom after Badr Safwan had sent to Madinah to kill the Prophet {{5}}, on the promise of taking responsibility for his debt and children. The hand that had gone with a knife was now asking the Prophet {{6}} for safety to save Safwan’s life. The Prophet {{7}} granted it. As a sign he gave his own turban, which had been on his head when he entered Makkah. Safwan returned. He said, give me two months’ time. The Prophet {{8}} said, you are given four months. Safwan accepted Islam later.{{9}}
blocks.33: In the list of death sentences announced, nine men. By al-Rahiq’s count four lost their lives, five were forgiven and came into Islam. Today we know which name ended up where, but that day being on the list did not mean being finished. The door of forgiveness was open even inside that list. We too make lists of people’s names: this one will never return, that one will never be right. Allah showed through His Messenger that a list is at best our reckoning. The real reckoning is in another’s hand.

footnotes.0: Sahih Muslim 1780 (Abu Hurayrah (RA); sahih): the Prophet {{1}} gave Zubayr charge of one flank, Khalid the other flank, and Abu ‘Ubaydah the infantry (husar); they took the middle of the valley, the Prophet {{2}} in one battalion (katibah); the Prophet {{3}} said to Abu Hurayrah, let no one come to me except an Ansari, call the Ansar; Quraysh had gathered some riff-raff (awbash); the Prophet {{4}}, placing one hand over the other, said, until you meet me at Safa. Sirah-based part: al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), pp. 659–661 (Khandamah: the gathering of ‘Ikrimah, Safwan and Suhayl; the dialogue and verses with Himas ibn Qays’s wife; twelve of Quraysh killed; Muslim martyrs Kurz ibn Jabir al-Fihri and Khunays ibn Khalid, who had gone by a separate path from the main body). This part is Sirah-based; the chain has not been verified in this dars, so it has come as a scene, not as evidence.
footnotes.1: al-Hakim, al-Mustadrak 4419, 8101 (from Anas ibn Malik (RA)); al-Hakim: sahih on the condition of Muslim; al-Dhahabi (Tarikh al-Islam 2/548): sahih. The narration ‘his beard was almost touching the middle of the howdah’ (Ibn Ishaq ← ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr) al-Albani called weak; in the dars the words of Anas (RA)’s sahih narration have been kept.
footnotes.2: Sahih al-Bukhari 4281, 5047; Sahih Muslim 794 (from ‘Abdullah ibn Mughaffal (RA); reciting Surah al-Fath on the she-camel’s back on the day of the conquest of Makkah, with tarji‘).
footnotes.3: Sahih al-Bukhari 4288 (‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas (RA)): the Prophet {{1}}, coming to Makkah, refused to enter because there were idols inside the House, by his order they were brought out, brought out were the pictures of Ibrahim and Isma‘il (AS), divination arrows in their hands; the Prophet {{2}} said, ‘May Allah destroy them! They know very well that they never sought fate with them.’ Then entering inside he said takbir in the corners of the house, did not pray (in Ibn ‘Abbas’s narration). In Bilal’s narration (Bukhari 397, 4289) he prayed two rak‘ahs; the word of the one who saw is preferred. Calling ‘Uthman ibn Talhah the keeper of the key and telling him to bring the key, entering with Usamah ibn Zayd, Bilal and ‘Uthman ibn Talhah (RA), spending a long time inside: Bukhari 4289 (Ibn ‘Umar (RA)).
footnotes.4: Sahih al-Bukhari 397 (Mujahid ← ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar (RA): finding Bilal standing between the two doors he asked, did the Prophet {{1}} pray inside the Ka‘bah? Bilal said, yes, two rak‘ahs, between the two pillars on the left as you enter; then coming out he prayed two rak‘ahs in front of the Ka‘bah); Sahih al-Bukhari 4289 (Ibn ‘Umar (RA): I forgot to ask how many rak‘ahs he had prayed).
footnotes.5: Sahih al-Bukhari 4288 (‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas (RA)): the Prophet {{1}}, coming to Makkah, refused to enter because there were idols inside the House, by his order they were brought out, brought out were the pictures of Ibrahim and Isma‘il (AS), divination arrows in their hands; the Prophet {{2}} said, ‘May Allah destroy them! They know very well that they never sought fate with them.’ Then entering inside he said takbir in the corners of the house, did not pray (in Ibn ‘Abbas’s narration). In Bilal’s narration (Bukhari 397, 4289) he prayed two rak‘ahs; the word of the one who saw is preferred. Calling ‘Uthman ibn Talhah the keeper of the key and telling him to bring the key, entering with Usamah ibn Zayd, Bilal and ‘Uthman ibn Talhah (RA), spending a long time inside: Bukhari 4289 (Ibn ‘Umar (RA)).
footnotes.6: Sahih al-Bukhari 397 (Mujahid ← ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar (RA): finding Bilal standing between the two doors he asked, did the Prophet {{1}} pray inside the Ka‘bah? Bilal said, yes, two rak‘ahs, between the two pillars on the left as you enter; then coming out he prayed two rak‘ahs in front of the Ka‘bah); Sahih al-Bukhari 4289 (Ibn ‘Umar (RA): I forgot to ask how many rak‘ahs he had prayed).
footnotes.7: Sunan Abi Dawud 4588 (from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr (RA)); al-Albani: hasan; Shu‘ayb Arna’ut: the chain is sahih. The three takbirs and the part ‘He has made His promise true … alone defeated all the factions’ are in the text quoted in al-Albani’s Irwa’ al-Ghalil 7/256 (the chain is sahih); the account of speaking while standing on the steps of the Ka‘bah is in the narration of Musnad Ahmad as verified by Ahmad Shakir (the chain is sahih).
footnotes.8: Ibn Ishaq ← Ibn Hisham, ‘Fath Makkah’ (the question to Quraysh at the door of the Ka‘bah and ‘idhhabu fa-antumu al-tulaqa’’). ⚠ The chain of these specific sentences is weak: al-Albani said, I did not find any sahih chain for it, it came as mu‘dal in Ibn Hisham (al-Ta‘liqat al-Radiyyah 3/475; Silsilah Da‘ifah 1163). It has been kept as a scene, not as evidence. But the incident of general forgiveness for the people of Makkah is itself established by a sahih chain: the safety announcement of Sahih Muslim 1780; and those who accepted Islam at the conquest of Makkah were later called by the name ‘tulaqa’’ (the freed), as came in the narration of Hunayn (Sahih al-Bukhari 4337).
footnotes.9: Sirah-based: al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), pp. 664–665 (Ibn Ishaq’s narration). Sirah-based; the chain has not been verified in this dars, so it has come as a scene, not as evidence. A separate sahih chain for Bilal (RA)’s adhan on the roof of the Ka‘bah has not been verified in this dars; the incident of the adhan on the roof is touched in one line of Dars 1. ‘Attab ibn Usayd and al-Harith ibn Hisham accepted Islam later.
footnotes.10: Sunan Abi Dawud 4359 (from Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas (RA); al-Albani: sahih), Mustadrak al-Hakim 4414 (sahih on the condition of Muslim); Sahih al-Jami‘ 2426 (al-Albani: ‘it does not befit a prophet to have a treachery of the eyes’: sahih). ‘Abdullah ibn Sa‘d was ‘Uthman (RA)’s foster brother.
footnotes.11: Sunan Abi Dawud 4359 (from Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas (RA); al-Albani: sahih), Mustadrak al-Hakim 4414 (sahih on the condition of Muslim); Sahih al-Jami‘ 2426 (al-Albani: ‘it does not befit a prophet to have a treachery of the eyes’: sahih). ‘Abdullah ibn Sa‘d was ‘Uthman (RA)’s foster brother.
footnotes.12: Sunan Abi Dawud 2683 (Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas (RA): ‘on the day of the conquest of Makkah the Prophet {{1}} gave safety to everyone except four men and two women’; Arna’ut: the chain of al-Daraqutni 3022 is hasan; in his note on Zad al-Ma‘ad 5/54 he said, the narrator Asbat ibn Nasr is saduq but errs often; a sahih form is also in al-Daraqutni 4344 and al-Hakim 2364); Sahih al-Bukhari 4286 (Anas (RA)): Ibn Khatal was hanging on to the cloth of the Ka‘bah, the Prophet {{2}} said, ‘kill him.’ Malik says, the Prophet {{3}} was not in ihram then. Sirah-based part: al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), pp. 665–667 (the list of nine men: ‘Abd al-‘Uzza ibn Khatal, ‘Abdullah ibn Sa‘d ibn Abi Sarh, ‘Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, al-Harith ibn Nufayl ibn Wahb, Miqyas ibn Subabah, Habbar ibn al-Aswad, the two slave-girls of Ibn Khatal, Sarah; in one narration four were killed, the rest were forgiven; by Ibn Ishaq’s count eight men and six women; Fath al-Bari 8/11–12).
footnotes.13: Sirah-based: al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), pp. 666–668 (‘Ikrimah: fled on the road to Yemen, his wife Umm Hakim bint al-Harith asked for safety and herself went and brought him back; Safwan: his name was not on the list, fleeing in fear by way of Jeddah on the road to Yemen; when ‘Umayr ibn Wahb al-Jumahi asked for safety, the Prophet {{1}} gave him the turban from his head as a sign; when Safwan asked for two months’ time, he said, you are given four months; later accepted Islam). Mustadrak al-Hakim 5138 (the incident of ‘Ikrimah; the narrators are reliable, al-Haythami: its men are thiqah); the part ‘marhaban bi al-rakib al-muhajir’ of al-Hakim 5142 and al-Tirmidhi is munqati‘ (al-Dhahabi, al-Haythami), so it has not been brought into this dars. The earlier incident of ‘Umayr and Safwan is in Dars 15. Sirah-based; the chain has not been verified in this dars, so it has come as a scene, not as evidence.

quiz.q: What is understood about boasting with the mouth and the truth of the battlefield from the incident of Khandamah?
o: The door of forgiveness is open even inside the list
Boasting is easy with the mouth; the weight is known when one comes face to face
Even in the work of truth not everything is to be told to everyone
Entering with a bowed head is the etiquette of victory, a sign of humility
quiz.e: Himas made the most weapons, and also fled first of all.

quiz.q: In Anas’s (RA) narration, how did the Prophet ﷺ enter Makkah?
o: Chin on the howdah, in humility
On horseback, in armour, sword in hand
quiz.e: With his chin on the howdah, bowed, in humility.

quiz.q: Which surah was the Prophet ﷺ reciting on entering Makkah?
quiz.e: Sahih al-Bukhari 4281.

quiz.q: What do the recitation of Surah al-Fath and the bowed head at the moment of victory signify?
o: Victory is Allah’s, not for arrogance
He was cautious for fear of the enemy
He was expressing grievance against the people of Makkah
quiz.e: The Qur’an on the lips, the head bowed.

quiz.q: On a day of good exam results or promotion at work, what is the Prophet’s ﷺ example?
o: Holding a big event to show standing, so everyone knows
quiz.e: On the day of victory, the bowed head and the Qur’an.

quiz.q: What was in the hands of the pictures of Ibrahim and Isma‘il (AS) brought out from inside the Ka‘bah?
quiz.e: Bukhari 4288.

quiz.q: Which two duties were kept in force in the sermon at the door of the Ka‘bah?
o: Service of the Ka‘bah and giving water to the pilgrims
The duty of Quraysh’s old council
quiz.e: Sidanat al-Bayt and siqayat al-hajj.

quiz.q: By what name were those who accepted Islam at the conquest of Makkah later called?
quiz.e: Tulaqa’, the freed.

quiz.q: ‘Every claim of blood of the Jahiliyyah is beneath my feet’; what is the social significance of this?
o: Confiscation of all of Quraysh’s wealth
Breaking the chain of revenge from generation to generation
The decision to send all the leaders of Makkah into exile
quiz.e: The son used to take revenge for the father’s blood; that cycle ended.

quiz.q: Though the chain of the sentence ‘Go, you are free’ is weak, how is the incident of general forgiveness established?
o: It is not established in any way
Only in a line of poetry
Only in the speculation of later historians
In the safety announcement of Sahih Muslim
quiz.e: Sahih Muslim 1780; and the name ‘tulaqa’’ is also proof.

quiz.q: The new generation too is carrying on an enmity from an old family dispute; what is the lesson of this dars?
o: Putting the old claims beneath the feet and ending it
Writing the dispute down so the next generation also does not forget
quiz.e: The Jahiliyyah claims of blood beneath the feet.

quiz.q: In the victory speech, first the praise of Allah, then settling old disputes; what is the application of this in a family reconciliation meeting?
o: Naming the guilty at the very start
Laying out the detailed account of everyone’s old wrongs
Gratitude at the start, then ending the old accounts
quiz.e: The order of the sermon at the Ka‘bah’s door.

quiz.q: The One from whom even hidden words are not concealed, whispering before Him; in which incident is this picture?
o: The incident of Safwan receiving the turban
The dialogue and verses with Himas’s wife
Abu Sufyan’s announcement of renewing the treaty
quiz.e: The Prophet ﷺ told their words one by one.

quiz.q: As a sign of safety for Safwan ibn Umayyah, what did the Prophet ﷺ give ‘Umayr ibn Wahb?
quiz.e: That turban which had been on his head when entering Makkah; Sirah-based.

quiz.q: After receiving safety, how many months’ time did Safwan ibn Umayyah ask for, and how many did he get?
quiz.e: The Prophet ﷺ said, you are given four months.

quiz.q: In the incident of Ibn Abi Sarh, what does the statement ‘it does not befit a prophet to deceive with the eyes’ teach?
o: Keeping the head bowed even on the day of victory
Keeping dignity by making Abu Sufyan’s house a refuge
Breaking the fast on a journey and showing it before everyone
What is in the mind is on the tongue; no deceit by hints
quiz.e: Abu Dawud 4359.

porbos.title: The Ansar’s Worry • Hind and Abu Quhafah • The Days After the Victory • In Crowds • Final Word

blocks.1: Makkah was conquered. The Ansar began to whisper among themselves; the man has felt the pull of his own city, affection for his relatives has stirred. Now perhaps he will stay right here. Through revelation the Prophet {{1}} came to know. He called the Ansar and asked, have you said such a thing? They admitted it. He said,
blocks.3: Never. I am the servant of Allah and His Messenger. I migrated to Allah and to you. My living is with your living, my dying with your dying.{{1}}
blocks.4: The Ansar came forward weeping. They said, by Allah, what we said was only out of attachment to Allah and His Messenger, out of fear of losing him. The Prophet {{1}} said, Allah and His Messenger affirm you as truthful, they accept your excuse. On the day the city of his birth, where the Ka‘bah is, came into his hands, he did not forget who had given him shelter. It is easy to make the companions of the days of hardship strangers in the days of ease; he did not do that. When a new opportunity comes today, do I not push the old faithful people behind for it tomorrow?
blocks.6: Among those who accepted Islam was Hind bint ‘Utbah (RA); who at Uhud had taken Hamzah’s (RA) liver into her mouth. Coming to the Prophet {{1}} she said,
blocks.8: O Messenger of Allah, there was no household on the face of the earth whose humiliation was dearer to me than the humiliation of the people of your household. And today there is no household on the face of the earth whose honour is dearer to me than the honour of the people of your household. The Prophet {{1}} said, by the One in whose hand is my soul, it will increase further.{{2}}
blocks.9: In one day a heart turned upside down; the household whose humiliation was dearest, the honour of that very household became dearest. Forgiveness does not merely let the enemy go; sometimes it turns the enemy into a friend.
blocks.11: Abu Bakr (RA) brought his old, sightless father Abu Quhafah, leading him by the hand, to the Prophet {{1}}. The Prophet {{2}} said, you should have left the old man at home; I would have gone to him.{{3}}
blocks.12: The Prophet {{1}} seated him in front, stroked his chest and gave him the call to Islam, and Abu Quhafah (RA) accepted Islam. His head and beard were completely white. The Prophet {{2}} said, dye this white hair with something.{{3}}
blocks.13: The busiest day of the victory. Yet he felt bad that a blind old man had had to walk to come. Respect for age, respect for a companion’s father; in the excuse of busyness these were not lost.
blocks.15: The next day the Prophet {{1}} stood to give a sermon. Abu Shurayh al-‘Adawi (RA) used to say later, my two ears heard, my heart remembered, my two eyes saw, when he said this. He praised Allah, then said,
blocks.17: Allah made Makkah sacred, people did not. For one who believes in Allah and the Last Day, it is not lawful to shed blood here, nor to cut down a tree. If anyone makes the fighting of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ an excuse, tell him, Allah had permitted His Messenger, He did not permit you. I was permitted for one hour of the day. Today its sanctity is again as it was yesterday. Let the one present convey it to the one absent.{{1}}
blocks.19: In Makkah there was permission for war for one hour. As soon as the hour ended, the announcement: today again sacred as before. The hand that had the sword returned it. On the very first day after the victory the limit was announced from the victor’s mouth. As much as the power, that much is the limit; because power is never one’s own. He announced another thing too,
blocks.21: After today, until the Day of Resurrection, no Qurayshi will be bound and killed.{{1}}
blocks.23: The leaders of the enemies were then unarmed before him. The chance to bind and kill was in hand. That door of chance he shut with his own mouth. Usamah ibn Zayd (RA) asked, O Messenger of Allah, where will you stay tomorrow? His own city, his own home. The Prophet {{1}} said,
blocks.27: Whatever houses there were, after the hijrah they had gone into ‘Aqil’s hands. The Prophet {{1}} did not rush after that house. The tent was pitched at Hajun. The house he had left for Allah, even on the day of victory the thought of taking it back did not occupy him. We often rush, when we get the chance, to take back first of all what we have left behind. When power and opportunity come into hand, it is one’s own lost things that come to mind first. He remembered first of all: this is the day of the city’s sanctity. Makkah became a city of the Muslims. So after the conquest the command to migrate from Makkah no longer remained. The Prophet {{2}} said,
blocks.29: After the conquest of Makkah there is no hijrah; there is jihad and intention. And when you are called to set out, set out.{{1}}
blocks.31: When the place changes the name of the deed changes. In place of hijrah came jihad and intention. The intention which, when it is there, does not require leaving the house, yet when the call comes does not hesitate to leave the house. On the morning of the victory Umm Hani (RA) went and saw the Prophet {{1}} bathing, his daughter Fatimah (RA) holding up a curtain. After the bath the Prophet {{2}}, wrapped in a single cloth, prayed eight rak‘ahs. Umm Hani says, it was the time of Duha.{{3}}
blocks.32: On the morning of the victory, no festival; eight rak‘ahs of prayer. After conquering a city the first deed was sujud. After some great success we first give the news, take pictures, celebrate. He first stood before Allah. He stayed nineteen days in Makkah. He prayed two rak‘ahs at a time. His own birthplace, yet in the city he had left by hijrah, the prayer of a traveller.{{1}}
blocks.34: After the conquest of Makkah the tribes of Arabia seemed to break out of waiting. All along they had been watching who would win in the fight between Quraysh and Muhammad. Now they began to come in crowds. The Qur’an had told of this day beforehand in this way,
blocks.36: When the help of Allah and the victory come, and you see people entering the religion of Allah in crowds, then glorify your Lord with His praise and seek His forgiveness. Surely He is the Most Forgiving.{{1}}
blocks.37: The command of the day of victory is not festival, but tasbih and istighfar. And Ibn ‘Abbas (RA) saw one more thing in this surah; the work has come to completion, the time of farewell too is near.{{1}}
blocks.38: When a big work is finished people usually count their own achievement. The Qur’an taught the opposite reckoning; praise is Allah’s, and asking forgiveness for oneself.
blocks.40: From the days of the conquest of Makkah a few pictures stay before the eye. The water vessel held up beside the spring of Kadid. The cousin who wanted to set out with his son’s hand to die, and the Prophet’s slap on his chest, you are the one who drove me out. The ten thousand fires of Marr al-Zahran, and the declaring of Abu Sufyan’s house a refuge. Entering with a bowed head, chin on the howdah, reciting Surah al-Fath. At the door of the Ka‘bah, all the claims of blood of Jahiliyyah beneath the feet. The Ansar’s weeping, and in answer, my living and dying are with you. Hind’s heart turned upside down. For blind Abu Quhafah, I would have gone myself. Abu Sufyan’s running about in Madinah and ‘Ali’s small answer, the decision has been made. Inside the Ka‘bah the pictures drawn in the name of Ibrahim (AS), without removing which he did not set foot in the house. Withholding his hand three times for Ibn Abi Sarh, and then saying, deceit by a hint is not for me. For Safwan his own turban, and saying, you are given four months. The next day’s sermon: Makkah is sacred, today again as before. Instead of rushing in search of the house that had gone into ‘Aqil’s hands, a tent at Hajun. On the morning of the victory, eight rak‘ahs of prayer. When power comes into hand, people change. Those at whose hands I suffered year after year, when they come into my fist, what do I do; the test is exactly there. So take away one deed from today’s dars.
blocks.42: Even with twenty years’ enemies in his fist, the Prophet {{1}} did not take revenge; on the day of victory he entered Makkah with a bowed head. Today I will ask myself a question: those from whom I have suffered, if they come into my fist, what will I do? Whatever chance of revenge I have in hand today, I will let it go; I will not keep this door of forgiveness shut from today.

footnotes.0: Sahih Muslim 1780 (from Abu Hurayrah (RA); the Ansar’s words, the revelation, ‘my living is with your living, my dying with your dying’, the Ansar’s weeping and ‘Allah and His Messenger affirm you as truthful, accept your excuse’). Al-Albani, Fiqh al-Sirah p. 399: sahih, Muslim brought it with a connected chain.
footnotes.1: Sahih al-Bukhari 7161 (from ‘A’ishah (RA)); the same hadith in Bukhari 3825 in mu‘allaq form. The words of the Prophet’s {{1}} reply: ‘wa aydan, wa-lladhi nafsi bi-yadihi’; Ibn Hajar explained its meaning as, this love of yours will increase further.
footnotes.2: Musnad Ahmad 26956 (from Asma’ bint Abi Bakr (RA)); Shu‘ayb Arna’ut: the chain is hasan; Ibn Hajar (al-Isabah 2/461): the chain is sahih. The Prophet {{1}} stroking his chest and giving the call to Islam, and his accepting Islam, is also in this narration.
footnotes.3: Sahih Muslim 2102 (from Jabir ibn ‘Abdillah (RA); Abu Quhafah’s head and beard like white thaghamah flowers, ‘change this with something’). The additional sentence about avoiding black has discussion among the hadith scholars, so it has not been kept in the dars.

quiz.q: Thinking what, did the Ansar fall into worry?
o: The Prophet ﷺ would stay in Makkah
Their leadership would be taken away from now on
quiz.e: That out of the pull of the city and affection for relatives he would stay.

quiz.q: ‘My living and dying are with you’; what does this express?
o: Not forgetting the companions of hardship in days of ease
A temporary promise as a political strategy of Madinah
quiz.e: He did not leave those who had given shelter.

quiz.q: Hearing the Ansar’s excuse, what did the Prophet ﷺ say?
o: Allah and His Messenger affirm you as truthful
Your share of spoils will be reduced for your suspicion
quiz.e: ‘They affirm you as truthful, accept your excuse.’

quiz.q: A good opportunity has come in a new job; what do I do with the companions of old hard times?
o: Give my mind only to the new circle
Keep contact with them only when needed, not at other times
quiz.e: ‘My living and dying are with you.’

quiz.q: In a day of danger someone wept for me, and out of a wrong fear also spoke harsh words; what does the incident of the Ansar teach?
o: Cutting off the relationship over harsh words
Arranging severe punishment without hearing the excuse, so that a lesson is learned
quiz.e: ‘He accepts your excuse.’

quiz.q: Whispering is going on within the team about someone’s mistake; in the incident of the Ansar what did the Prophet ﷺ do?
o: Calling them directly, talking and settling it
Arranging for others to keep watch on them
quiz.e: He called and asked, have you said this?

quiz.q: Hind bint ‘Utbah (RA) said whose household’s honour was dearest to her?
quiz.e: Today the honour of your household is the dearest.

quiz.q: Abu Quhafah (RA) was whose father?
quiz.e: The father of Abu Bakr (RA).

quiz.q: Seeing Abu Quhafah’s white hair, what did the Prophet ﷺ say?
quiz.e: Sahih Muslim 2102.

quiz.q: From Hind’s change, which aspect of forgiveness becomes clear?
o: Forgiveness is an expression of weakness
Forgiveness makes even an enemy a friend
Forgiveness is due only to relatives
If you forgive, the enemy becomes bolder and strikes again
quiz.e: In one day a heart turned upside down.

quiz.q: ‘Leave the old man at home, I would have gone’; what is the lesson of this?
o: The old are forbidden to come to gatherings
Respect for age even in busyness
A sick person should never be invited
quiz.e: Even on the busy day of the victory, the hardship of a blind old man made him feel bad.

quiz.q: Someone who was earlier hostile to me is now showing love; what did the Prophet ﷺ do with Hind?
o: Keeping her at a distance with suspicion
Bringing up old matters and taunting
Ignoring her love and silently moving away
quiz.e: ‘By the One in whose hand is my soul, it will increase.’

quiz.q: A friend’s elderly father wants to take the trouble to come to meet me; according to this dars what should be done?
o: Settling it by phone alone, no need to meet
quiz.e: ‘I would have gone to him.’

quiz.q: In the sermon narrated by Abu Shurayh (RA), what was the announcement about Makkah?
o: No Qurayshi will be bound and killed again
All claims of blood of Jahiliyyah beneath the feet
Today there is no blame or rebuke upon you
The permission to fight was for one hour, today it is again sacred
quiz.e: Bukhari 104.

quiz.q: What does ‘after the conquest there is no hijrah; there is jihad and intention’ teach?
o: When the place changes the name of the deed changes, the intention remains
The whispers of enemies are not hidden from the Prophet ﷺ
Eight rak‘ahs on the morning of the victory
Claims of blood of Jahiliyyah beneath the feet
quiz.e: Bukhari 2783.

quiz.q: On the morning of victory, not festival first but standing before Allah first; which incident matches this?
o: Drinking water in daytime at Kadid
The Prophet’s ﷺ tent being pitched at Hajun
Entering bowed with the chin on the camel’s howdah
Eight rak‘ahs of prayer in Umm Hani’s house
quiz.e: Bukhari 357.

quiz.q: What does Surah al-Nasr say to do after victory?
o: Making a list of enemies and trying them
quiz.e: Glorifying with praise and seeking forgiveness.

quiz.q: What hint did Ibn ‘Abbas (RA) see in Surah al-Nasr?
o: The capital will move from Madinah
The rules of Hajj will soon change completely
The Prophet’s ﷺ farewell is near
quiz.e: The work complete, the farewell near.

quiz.q: A big project has ended successfully; according to the lesson of Surah al-Nasr what is the first deed?
o: Making a list of colleagues’ mistakes and telling everyone
quiz.e: After victory, tasbih and istighfar.

quiz.q: Someone who hurt me a lot is dependent on me today; according to the practical resolve what will I do?
o: Let go of the chance of revenge
Have someone else take the revenge
Help him, but each time reminding him of old matters
quiz.e: Letting go of the chance of revenge in hand.
